rule: GOAL: Bring both red pads on the white piece onto the matching pads on the green piece. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the white piece; Space turned it clockwise. RULE: The green piece stayed fixed, so the white piece had to turn and slide into place. TRAP: Assuming the pads already faced the right way led to wasted movement.

GOAL: Remove pegs by jumping until only one peg remains. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a highlighted empty cell to land there. RULE: A peg jumps straight over a neighboring peg into an empty cell, removing the peg it crossed. TRAP: Thinking the green cells were lights to toggle wasted time; they were pegs to move.

GOAL: Put one green piece on each outlined square. CONTROLS: Arrow keys moved the selected piece; clicking the other piece switched control. RULE: Bumping the other piece sent it across the purple strip while the selected piece stayed behind. TRAP: Treating the black-centered piece as a crate to push step by step wasted time.

GOAL: Connect all four pieces by lining up their matching red pads. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece, space turned it clockwise, and clicking selected a piece, making it white. RULE: Matching pads had to overlap exactly; gray pads confirmed a connection. Each piece still moved independently. TRAP: Thinking connected pieces would move together wasted time. Moving one could break its connections.

GOAL: Put all four pieces on matching outlines, launching two across purple strips. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it. Arrows move the selected piece one step; contact pushes another piece. RULE: A pushed piece jumps five tiles, letting it cross purple that ordinary movement cannot cross. TRAP: Thinking every piece could reach its outline by walking wasted time; some needed another piece to launch them.

GOAL: Arrange the pieces so all matching red contact pads overlap. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; space turned it clockwise; clicking selected a piece and revealed its color and pads. RULE: Overlapping pads turned gray to confirm a connection, but connected pieces still moved independently. TRAP: Treating charcoal shapes as obstacles wasted time; they were unselected pieces with hidden pads.

GOAL: Put both yellow crosses on their matching outlines and the green square on its square outline. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the green square one step or pushed a cross it touched. RULE: A completed push sent a cross five tiles, so count the landing space rather than expecting a small nudge. TRAP: Believing a cross had to be pushed through its center wasted time; touching an arm

GOAL: Leave just one peg in total, not one in each separate group. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then its landing spot to jump. Arrow keys move the orange cell along the track, carrying any peg aboard. Purple retries the level. RULE: The orange square is a movable landing cell. Use it to carry a peg between groups and make the final jump. TRAP: Treating the orange square as a button hid its real purpose.

GOAL: Arrange all four pieces so every pad meets a matching pad, without overlapping solid bodies. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece and reveal its pads. Arrows move it; space turns it a quarter turn. RULE: Pads connect when they overlap exactly and turn gray. Hidden pads still matter, so inspect every piece. TRAP: Connected pieces do not move together. Moving one can break a connection you already made.

GOAL: Leave one peg by clearing the fixed groups and carrying pegs between them. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then a highlighted landing cell to jump. Arrow keys moved both orange carriers along their tracks. RULE: A jump crossed one neighboring peg into an empty cell and removed the crossed peg. Carriers could hold and transport pegs. TRAP: Assuming ordinary jumps could connect every group wasted time; some gaps needed a carrier.

GOAL: Put both green squares and the yellow cross on their matching outlines. CONTROLS: Click a green square to select it; use arrows to move it and push other pieces. The yellow cross cannot be selected. RULE: Launches can cross purple dividers and travel farther to reach valid ground; boundaries can shorten them. TRAP: Believing every launch moved exactly five spaces led to wasted planning.

GOAL: Find the right sequence of moves and actions to clear the level. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the blue bar; Space was the action key, not another direction. RULE: Position alone was not enough; the clear used three arrow presses and four Space presses. TRAP: Treating Space as useless led to sweeping positions until the action budget ran out.

GOAL: Leave just one green peg by linking separate areas with moving carriers. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then its landing space to jump. Select a carrier and use arrow keys to move it along its track. RULE: Jumped green pegs disappear; purple supports stay. Carriers can carry pegs or provide landing spaces across gaps. TRAP: Treating purple supports like removable pegs leads to bad plans; they remain available for later jumps.

GOAL: Get the green square out of the purple corridor and onto its matching outline. CONTROLS: The arrows moved the square; moving into a red object could push it. RULE: The red bumpers fired every third action, so each move changed when it was safe to approach. TRAP: Treating a bumper as a fixed hazard wasted time. Pushing it away could clear the route.

GOAL: Reduce all the green pegs to one, including those in panels revealed later. CONTROLS: Click a green peg, then its landing space to jump. Arrow keys moved both carriers along their tracks. RULE: Every jump needed a peg or purple support between takeoff and an empty landing space; a carrier could supply that landing. TRAP: An empty carrier beside a peg was not enough to receive it. There still had to be something to jump over.

GOAL: Grow the yellow piece fully, then arrange the pieces so every red pad has a matching contact. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece. Space rotated it. Clicking selected a piece; clicking its white handle grew it. RULE: Pads connected by exact overlap, not by touching edges. Growing yellow added the contacts needed to finish. TRAP: Treating the white square as a contact instead of a growth handle made the starting shapes seem impossible to solve.

GOAL: Push the cross onto its outline and guide the square to its goal. CONTROLS: The arrows moved the square and pushed the cross or movable bumpers when approached from the side. RULE: Bumpers fired in pulses, launching an aligned square across purple gaps. Cross their firing path just after a pulse. TRAP: Assuming distance from a bumper meant safety wasted time. Its firing path reached farther than expected; timing mattered more.

GOAL: Fill the three spaces in the blue outline with the three blue blocks. CONTROLS: Arrows moved your piece and any block it held. Space grabbed the block you faced. RULE: Stand beside a block and face it to grab it; touching it was not enough. TRAP: Treating the blue centers as switches or things to collect wasted time.

GOAL: Get all five blue blocks into the destination before the action budget ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved and turned the green player. Space grabbed or released a block in front, or waited when empty. RULE: The orange helper delivered blocks on its own, so leaving its route clear let it finish the job. TRAP: Thinking every block needed your help led to needless moves and wasted the budget.

GOAL: Reduce the green pegs to one by linking the separated branches. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then its landing spot to jump. Arrow keys moved the carriers, even when red was selected. RULE: Jumps needed a peg to cross and an empty landing spot. Carriers followed their tracks. TRAP: Believing

GOAL: Get all five blocks delivered by the helper before time ran out. CONTROLS: Movement changed position and facing; grab lifted or dropped an adjacent block; waiting let the helper work. RULE: The striped barrier stopped you, but blocks could be held inside it and left for the helper to collect from the other side. TRAP: Believing you could walk through the barrier while carrying a

GOAL: Move the bars so a fired shot could reach the opening. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, use arrows to move it, and press space to fire. RULE: Moving and firing used a limited budget, with shots costing much more than moves. TRAP: Assuming firing always selected the long bar again led to moving the wrong bar.

GOAL: Arrange the three bars so one shot reaches all three cup openings. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, use arrows to move it, and press space to fire. RULE: Bars split the shot into paths just outside their ends, so line those paths up with the openings. TRAP: Assuming space always selected the long bar again led to moving the wrong bar.

GOAL: Guide the downward streams into all four cups by arranging the bars. CONTROLS: Click to select a bar, use arrows to move it sideways or vertically, and press space to test the flow. RULE: A stream hitting a bar splits into paths just beyond both ends. Extra streams may leave the board without spoiling the solution. TRAP: Searching only sideways moves wasted time; changing the bars’ heights changed which bars the streams met first.

GOAL: Feed both rising streams into all four cups, including the sideways cup. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece, use arrow keys to move it, and press space to send the streams. RULE: Bars split streams, while the elbow turns a branch sideways. Split one source before the elbow and split its other branch again. TRAP: Assuming the elbow’s drawn leg marked its inlet wasted a test. Moving only the elbow one step right fixed the route.

GOAL: Get all six cargo blocks into the destination slots with help from the helpers. CONTROLS: Direction keys moved you and positioned cargo; space advanced time for the helpers. RULE: Helpers needed cargo on a wall they could reach. Side walls served the side helpers; the bottom helper needed cargo on the bottom wall. TRAP: Believing every wall was an

GOAL: Get the green peg into the final alcove by arranging carriers and support pegs. CONTROLS: Arrows moved all carriers with room on their tracks. Clicks selected a movable peg and its landing place. RULE: A peg could jump over one nearby peg onto an empty support two spaces away. Purple pegs served as supports, not selectable pieces. TRAP: Treating carriers as independently controlled wasted time; every arrow could move several at once.

GOAL: Carry the green piece between boards and carriers to capture the remaining green. CONTROLS: Click a piece, then its landing space to jump. Arrow keys moved the carriers, sometimes together. RULE: Jumps needed an occupied middle space and an empty landing space; blue supports stayed put. TRAP: Thinking jumps pushed blue pieces aside led to plans that could not work.

GOAL: Bring the greens from two panels together and leave just one green. CONTROLS: Click to make jumps and move the carrier along its track. RULE: Only green jumping over green removed a green. Blue pieces and fixed purple supports helped make routes. TRAP: The panel’s gap looked like a carrier stop, but it was not. Transfer green at the notch instead.

GOAL: Get all six blocks to the target through the helper before the action limit. CONTROLS: Movement also set your facing; grab and release handled blocks; space waited while the helper worked. RULE: Carried blocks kept their offset from you, so both you and the load needed a clear path. TRAP: Believing the direct route would fit wasted moves. Use the passage handoff, then stay out of

GOAL: Bring both cargo blocks through the narrow wall passage and into the blue target. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you and carried held cargo; space picked up or set down blocks and removed the nearby thief. RULE: The purple thief could steal delivered cargo, so removing it made deliveries safe. TRAP: Assuming the purple figure was another helper wasted time and let it take a block.

GOAL: Get both green pieces onto the dark outlined targets. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it; its white center shows selection. Arrows move the selected piece one space. RULE: Moving into the other piece launches it, letting it cross the purple barrier. TRAP: Thinking every move was a normal step hid the key: use one piece to launch the other.

GOAL: Move the white piece so both red pads meet the fixed green piece’s pads. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the white piece; Space turned it clockwise. RULE: Both pad pairs had to line up, with the pads facing each other. TRAP: Thinking the pads could connect while facing the same way cost extra turns.

GOAL: Leave just one green peg on the board. CONTROLS: Click a peg to select it, then click a highlighted empty hole to jump there. RULE: A legal jump passes straight over a neighboring peg into an empty hole and removes the jumped peg. TRAP: Thinking any empty hole was a valid landing spot, rather than checking the highlighted choices.
GOAL: Position the blue bar to guide the magenta source into the yellow cups. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the bar. Space spent budget but caused no visible

GOAL: Place the blue bar to guide the magenta flow into both yellow cups. CONTROLS: Arrows shifted the bar; Space changed the budget strip; the click’s role was unclear. RULE: Keep the source over the bar’s middle and its ends above the cup openings. TRAP: Expecting Space alone to release the flow before the bar was aligned

GOAL: Leave one peg by linking the two separated groups with the orange carrier. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the carrier along its track. Click a peg, then its landing hole, to jump. RULE: Jump over a neighboring peg into an empty hole to remove it. The carrier could hold and transport a peg. TRAP: Expecting the moved peg to stay selected wasted clicks; each jump cleared the selection.

GOAL: Join all four pieces so every red pad meets a matching pad. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece, use arrows to move it, and press Space to turn it clockwise. RULE: Pads must meet in opposing pairs, without the solid parts of pieces overlapping. TRAP: Assuming only the white piece could move hid the option to select and move the others.

GOAL: Put all four pieces into their matching outlines, including those across purple barriers. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece. Use arrows to move it; bump another piece to launch it. RULE: Launches can carry pieces across purple barriers and push other pieces along the path. TRAP: Assuming every launch travels five tiles; that distance was not a fixed rule.

GOAL: Move the bars so rays from the sources reach every yellow cup. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it, use arrows to shift it, and press Space to fire. RULE: A ray hitting a bar splits into rays just beyond both ends; extra rays may miss the cups. TRAP: Assuming every ray had to land in a cup wasted time.

GOAL: Put both yellow crosses on their matching outlines and park the green launcher on its square target. CONTROLS: Clicking selected the green launcher; arrows moved it. An arrow into a cross launched that cross. RULE: Each cross flew exactly five tiles while the launcher stayed put; contact with a cross arm was enough. TRAP: Believing the yellow crosses could be selected and moved directly wasted time.

GOAL: Join all three pieces so every connector pad meets a matching pad without solid parts overlapping. CONTROLS: Click to select a piece, use arrows to move it, and press Space to rotate it. RULE: Only the selected piece shows its color and pads; matched pads turn gray. TRAP: I mistook the charcoal pieces for obstacles or switched-off pieces. They were unselected pieces with hidden pads.

GOAL: Join all four pieces so every pad meets a pad on another piece, without overlapping solid parts. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, use arrows to move it, and press Space to rotate it. RULE: Only the selected piece showed its pads; the others stayed dark but still counted. TRAP: Thinking dark pieces were fixed obstacles or that their hidden pads had disappeared.

GOAL: Leave just one peg across all the connected boards, using moving cells to carry pegs between groups. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then an empty landing hole to jump. Arrow buttons move both carriers when their tracks allow. RULE: A jump crosses one neighboring peg into an empty hole and removes the crossed peg. Carriers can transport pegs. TRAP: Mistaking a scrolling view for a new level hid the fact that pegs still remained offscreen.

GOAL: Get the yellow cross onto its upper target and a green launcher onto the lower target. CONTROLS: Click a green launcher to select it. Arrows move it; contact launches another piece while the launcher stays put. RULE: Launches travel five tiles, extend across purple until the whole piece reaches safe floor, and stop early at boundaries. TRAP: Thinking you had to stand beneath the cross’s central stem wasted time; pushing beneath either arm also worked.

GOAL: Guide the green piece through the channel and onto its goal, past the orange and dark red structures. CONTROLS: The arrow keys moved the green piece and advanced the structures’ cycle. RULE: Timing mattered: an upward move could bounce the piece backward instead of moving it forward. TRAP: Treating the two-tone structures as ordinary movable blocks wasted time; their changing state mattered more than pushing them.

GOAL: Leave one green peg by clearing the linked groups and carrying the survivor back to the last peg. CONTROLS: Click a green peg, then its landing hole to jump. Arrow keys moved carriers along their tracks; the view scrolled with them. RULE: Jump over a piece into an empty hole. Jumped green pegs disappeared, but purple pieces stayed and could be reused. TRAP: Treating purple pieces as pegs to remove wasted time; they were permanent stepping stones.

GOAL: Arrange the pieces so every red pad connects with another red pad. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the selected piece; Space rotated it. Clicking a piece selected it; clicking its white square extended it. RULE: Only the selected piece showed its pads. Extending a piece changed its shape and added pads. TRAP: Treating the white square as ordinary body material led to searching arrangements before discovering the growth control.

GOAL: Move the bars so the rays reach all four cups. CONTROLS: Click a bar to select it. Arrows move it sideways or up and down. Space starts the ray attempt. RULE: The red ends and dark center move as one bar, but each side splits rays separately. Rays leaving the board disappear. TRAP: Assuming bars could only slide sideways hid the solution; moving a bar below the others changed the route.

GOAL: Carry all three blue blocks into the blue destination outline. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the player and carried block; space grabbed the block directly ahead. RULE: A block was delivered when carried into the destination; its border turned dark gray. TRAP: Expecting to press space again to drop each block added needless steps.

GOAL: Guide the green piece onto both yellow targets beyond the purple barrier. CONTROLS: Arrows moved the piece, pushed red blocks, and advanced their charge, even when movement was blocked. RULE: Charged red blocks pulsed, launching nearby pieces away and across purple barriers; gray walls still blocked travel. TRAP: I thought clicking empty floor would advance the charge. Only arrow actions did, so pressing against a wall was useful for waiting.

GOAL: Leave one green peg by joining scattered groups with jumps and moving carriers. CONTROLS: Click to select pieces and make jumps; use arrow keys to move the selected carrier along its track. RULE: Each jump needed an empty landing hole beyond a neighboring peg or purple stone, so carrier alignment mattered. TRAP: Assuming both carriers followed the same route wasted time; the purple carrier had its own track.

GOAL: Get all the blocks into the destination slots before the action budget ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved and turned you; space grabbed or released the block you faced. RULE: Carried blocks needed a clear path; other blocks and the helper could obstruct delivery. TRAP: Assuming the helper could finish alone wasted the budget. Carrying the farthest block yourself saved time.

GOAL: Reduce the green pegs to one, using the red helper and moving carriers to cross gaps. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then its landing spot to jump. Arrow keys move carriers along their tracks. RULE: Green jumping over green removes the jumped peg. Jumps involving the red helper or purple stepping stones leave them in place. TRAP: Two carrier cells side by side looked like one platform, but they moved independently along different tracks.

GOAL: Get all five blocks into the destination with help from the helper. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; space grabbed or released a block. RULE: The helper could collect blocks left in the barrier openings and carry them onward, so clear openings made handoffs work. TRAP: Thinking you had to carry every block to the destination yourself, instead of staging blocks for the helper.

GOAL: Bring the two green pegs together and jump one over the other, leaving one. CONTROLS: Click a peg and its landing spot to jump. Arrow buttons moved all carriers along their tracks. RULE: A jump needed a peg or purple stone to cross and an empty landing spot; an empty carrier could provide that spot. TRAP: Trying to position one carrier alone wasted time. All carriers moved together, and the purple stone could block the final landing.

GOAL: Get every block onto a destination, letting the helpers finish delivery. CONTROLS: Movement moved you; grabbing and releasing transferred blocks; space waited and advanced the helpers. RULE: Waiting was enough here: nine presses of space cleared the level. TRAP: Believing the helpers were stuck led to needless block transfers and rearranging that wasted the action budget.

GOAL: Leave just one green peg by bringing the separated greens together. CONTROLS: Click a peg, then its landing spot to jump. Arrow keys move carriers, not selected pegs. RULE: Jumped green pegs disappear; blue and purple supports stay. Blue pegs can also jump. TRAP: Assuming blue pegs were fixed hid the route. Moving them opened jumps onto carriers.

GOAL: Guide rays from the sources into every cup using splitters and a corner reflector. CONTROLS: Click a piece to select it, use arrows to move it, and press space to fire. RULE: A splitter sends an incoming ray out just beyond each end of its bar. TRAP: Assuming the corner reflected in the expected direction led to wasted shots and needless changes elsewhere.

GOAL: Get all six blocks into the destination before the action budget ran out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you; space grabbed or released a block. The helper worked on its own. RULE: You and the helper shared the paths, and delivered blocks could obstruct later trips. TRAP: Trusting the helper to fetch every distant block wasted the budget. Carrying far blocks yourself and clearing the destination saved time.

GOAL: Get both blocks into the destination, including the one the purple carrier took out. CONTROLS: Arrows moved you and any block you held. Space disabled the purple carrier when you faced it nearby. RULE: Carry a block at your side to fit through the narrow passage. TRAP: Assuming the purple piece was harmless wasted time; it could take a block already delivered.

GOAL: Remove the island’s green piece while leaving the carried green in place. CONTROLS: Click a piece and its landing space to jump. Move the carrier along its rail; pan to see hidden parts of the island. RULE: Jumps need a support and an empty landing. Shuttle the blue pair to guide the island green toward its final jump. TRAP: Assuming the carried green had to disembark wasted time

GOAL: Bring both blocks into the two spaces in the left destination. CONTROLS: Arrows moved and turned you; Space acted on what you faced, including disabling the purple carrier. RULE: The carrier could steal blocks, but disabling it left both blocks still and ready to deliver. TRAP: Chasing its last position wasted time because it could move between your turn and your Space press.

GOAL: Get every storage block into a destination before the action budget ran out. CONTROLS: Direction keys moved and turned you. Space grabbed or released a block, or disabled a thief within reach. RULE: Helpers kept hauling while you acted. Stopping thieves protected progress, but carrying one block yourself saved a crucial round trip. TRAP: Believing that stopping both thieves was enough. Waiting for the helpers alone still ran out the budget.
